fig2_stress.title: Survey effort and missing access points
fig2_stress.alt: Two panels: error relative to tuned kNN against share of reference points surveyed, and mean error against share of access points switched off.
shows: (a) Mean error relative to tuned kNN on the full survey of the same building, averaged over CETC331, HCXY and SYL; band from the lowest to the highest of the 10 draws. Large markers sit where each foundation model reaches the kNN level; the legend gives that share overall and per building.

(b) Mean error in metres averaged over the three buildings against the share of MAC columns switched off in the test file, 30 draws (0 to 9 from P1-E02, 10 to 29 from P1-E03); the shaded areas are the gap between the -105 and the NaN version of TabPFN and of LightGBM.
Six measured series per panel at most (FIGURE_TASTE II, B3); the models not drawn are printed by the generator.
fixed: Panel (a) legend was wider than the panel and ran off its left edge: rows rebuilt as two short lines, per-building crossings on the second line as rounded percentages.
Legends covered the 5% band and the LightGBM band: limits now come from the band extremes and the legends sit in head room I checked on the render.
The two x-axis labels collided in the middle of the figure: shorter labels and wider panel spacing.
Two legend boxes in (b) overlapped each other: merged into one box above every band.
kNN's row printed 'nan' while its 5% runs were missing: the row now prints n/a until the data exist.

On the final data the baselines legend in (a) covered the 10% to 25% curves: rebuilt as a compact box (5% to 100% ratios) stacked under the foundation-model box, with head room set from the band maximum.
A hyphen stood in for a minus sign in the shaded-gap row: replaced by a true minus.
limits: The corner between the baselines legend and the RF band at 10% was cropped and enlarged 2x on the final render: clear gap, glyphs intact. The other text regions were read at review resolution only.
Panel (a) averages ratios over three buildings; per-building crossing shares are in the legend and in P1-E02 metrics/e2_crossing.csv.

table1_full_survey.slot: Table I · drawn as a figure · P1-E01
table1_full_survey.title: Full-survey comparison in five configurations
table1_full_survey.alt: Table of mean positioning error for ten models in five configurations, with bars, ranks, cost and a bootstrap row.
shows: Mean error over seeds for every model and configuration, with the standard deviation over seeds and the 95th percentile underneath; the bar is the cell's error relative to the column's worst; the best cell of each column is bold.
Mean rank over the five configurations, fit plus predict seconds (median over configurations) and the median search time of the tuned baselines.
Bottom row: best foundation model minus best baseline, seed 0 of each, with the 95% bootstrap interval over test points (bold where the interval excludes zero).
fixed: Value bars overlapped the second line of each cell: bars moved under the text.
The last three column headers collided: wider columns and shorter headers.
The tuning column now says it is an upper bound (searches shared the nodes with other jobs).
limits: Search times were measured while other jobs shared the node; they are upper bounds (see P1-E01 RESULTS.md).

typeset_tables.slot: Tables I and II · one column each · LaTeX (booktabs)
typeset_tables.title: The two LaTeX tables as typeset in the IEEE template
typeset_tables.alt: Table I (mean error per model in the three main buildings, average, 95th percentile, time) and Table II (pipeline check and foundation-model cost) as they print in an IEEE two-column page.
shows: Table I: mean positioning error with the full survey, three main buildings, mean with the standard deviation over 5 seeds as subscript, the average, the average 95th percentile and the median fit plus predict time; best per column in bold.
Table II: the pipeline check against the dataset paper (mean and 95th percentile) and what the foundation models cost on HCXY (fit, predict, GPU memory).
Both are generated from the result files by code/p1/figs/tables.py; this image is a crop of the IEEE conference template page at 220 dpi.
fixed: Table I was 34.9 pt and Table II 6.2 pt wider than the 252 pt column: set in footnotesize, standard deviations as subscripts, tighter column separation (fixed in the generator, not in the emitted .tex).
Checked in the real IEEEtran class (textwidth 516 pt, columnwidth 252 pt): zero overfull boxes with every figure placed.
limits: Built with this machine's TeX Live fonts; the venue's authoritative build may shift widths slightly, and both tables keep some margin.

fig_cost_accuracy.title: What a fix costs and what it buys
fig_cost_accuracy.alt: Scatter of mean error relative to tuned kNN against fit plus predict time, with tuning time for the baselines.
shows: Every model in every configuration as a small mark (mean over seeds): seconds to fit and predict one test file against mean error relative to tuned kNN in that configuration, both on log axes.

Large haloed marks: each model's median over the five configurations. Tuned baselines also carry an open mark joined by a dotted line at the same error with their median search time added, the training step a foundation model does not have.
fixed: The LightGBM marker was clipped at the top edge: limits now padded from the data.
Tuning arrows were invisible (kNN's lay on the reference line, LightGBM's ran off the axis): replaced by open markers and the x range widened to include them.
The lower legend hid the TabPFN -105 point: room added below the data for that legend.
Rebuilt from scratch on the final data: range whiskers stretched to 4.2x (one configuration) and squeezed the data into a band; replaced by every configuration as its own mark on log axes.
Two legend boxes overlapped each other and then the data: merged into one box in head room above every mark.
limits: Search times are upper bounds (shared nodes).

fig_uncertainty.title: Are the predictive distributions calibrated?
fig_uncertainty.alt: Coverage of central predictive intervals against nominal level, and error by decile of predicted spread.
shows: (a) Share of test rows inside the central predictive interval against its nominal level, averaged over the two coordinates, seeds and five configurations; band: range over configurations.
(b) Mean error of the test rows in each decile of predicted spread, relative to the model's mean error; Spearman correlation between spread and error in the legend.
fixed: Panel (a) legend ran past the panel and hid the 95% points: moved under the curves with shorter rows.
Panel (b) legend covered the decile 9 and 10 bands and the y label: head room added above the bands.
limits: GP coverage comes from one run per configuration; the foundation models from five seeds.
Coverage is per coordinate; the joint coverage of both coordinates is in the Uncertainty table.

fig_scans_cost.title: How many scans per point, and what the context costs
fig_scans_cost.alt: Error against scans per reference point, and fit plus predict time against context rows.
shows: (a) Mean error against scans per reference point, relative to the same model with all 30 scans, averaged over HCXY and SYL; the dotted guide marks the 26-scan cap used for TabPFN on HCXY in P1-E01.
(b) Fit plus predict seconds against context rows for the foundation models; marker shape is the building, marker area the peak GPU memory; the dotted guide is TabPFN v2's 10,000-row limit.
fixed: The reference was 30 scans, which on HCXY is 11,370 rows, past TabPFN v2's 10,000-row limit, where TabPFN with NaN gets worse; the reference is now 26 scans, inside the limit in both buildings (and identical to the P1-E01 HCXY context).
Tick labels 26 and 30 collided: 26 is now marked by the dotted guide only.
The legend in (a) covered the top of the kNN band, and the legend in (b) a TabPFN point: head room added above the data.
The time axis printed 6x10^1 style labels: plain seconds; memory markers scaled down so TabICL's 52 GB squares no longer hide the line.
limits: kNN and GP use the seed-0 scan draw only (they have no randomness); the foundation models average five draws.
Timings were measured while other jobs shared the node; they show the trend with context size, not clean costs.
